_meta.description: Carbon and land-use reference values. Live values are fetched from the ADEME Agribalyse API at runtime; these are the cached fallbacks and the structural factors the API does not provide.
_meta.source: ADEME Agribalyse v3.x impact values (kg CO2e per kg product, climate change indicator) plus published soy land-use-change figures.
_meta.functional_unit_note: Comparing per kg of PRODUCT flatters pulses against soy meal, which is far more protein-dense. The engine therefore reports both per kg product AND per kg of crude protein, which is the honest basis for a feed substitution claim.

land_use_change.description: Imported South American soy meal carries a land-use-change burden that dominates its footprint. Excluding it, as some corporate inventories do, erases most of the advantage of substituting with a French pulse. The engine reports both.
land_use_change.note: Agribalyse and the EU PEF method include amortised LUC; the GHG Protocol Land Sector guidance treats it separately. Which convention the buyer uses changes the answer materially.

imported_food_pulse.description: The counterfactual for the HUMAN-FOOD fraction of the harvest. A graded lot does not displace Brazilian soybean meal - that is what the DOWNGRADED fraction displaces, through animal feed. A lot that passes retail specification displaces an imported pulse on a French plate, because that is what France currently eats: domestic production covers under half of French dry-pulse consumption.
imported_food_pulse.method: Transport differential only: (sea leg + overseas inland leg) for the import, minus the French farm-to-processor haul. The production footprints of a Canadian and a French lentil are both those of a rain-fed legume and are not reliably distinguishable in open data, so claiming a production advantage would be inventing one. Transport is the term that is genuinely origin-dependent, so it is the only term claimed.
imported_food_pulse.cross_check: Agribalyse's synthesis value for dried lentil puts 0.244 kg CO2e/kg on retail transport. The figures below come out materially BELOW that, because the overseas inland leg is costed as rail rather than road. Conservative by construction.
imported_food_pulse.caveat: A transport-only saving is small next to the feed-substitution figure, and deliberately so. The food-tier claim worth making is in TONNES of imports displaced from French plates, not in carbon. The engine reports both and does not blend them.
